Non-blocking: (a) payments-showcase.tsx repeats token='USDC' and decimals={6} about 11 times, and its timeline step labels repeat SAMPLE_STEPS and PAYMENT_STATUSES labels; move them to constants (SAMPLE_INVOICE.token exists). (c) useCopy (interactive.tsx:1464) has no catch for a clipboard rejection and does not clear its timer on unmount; the 1600ms timeout and Tooltip delayDuration=200 are raw durations, not tokens. (d) Dialog backdrop uses the default Tailwind backdrop-blur-sm, not --fw-blur-glass. (h) The kit's sample copy ('Arbitrum (planned)', the invented forwend.invoices.create API in CodeBlock) is fine on a private noindex page, but do not reuse it on the landing page in F006-F008.

(4) saved() treats any non-empty stored value as an explicit choice, while the init script ignores unknown values; edge case only.

notes: 2026-10-08 review fail by subagent: Shimmer sweep never crosses the block. packages/ui-web/src/components/motion.tsx:57 puts after:-translate-x-full on the ::after; in Tailwind 4.3.3 that sets the separate CSS 'translate' property (-100%), which adds to the keyframe 'transform' from packages/design-tokens/src/base.css:159-163 (fw-shimmer: to translateX(100%)). Net movement is -100% -> 0%, not -100% -> +100%. Browser evidence (localhost:3000/kit, sampled every 110ms): ::after translate stays '-100%' while transform goes 106 -> 255px (block width 256px) and then resets to 0. So the 70% surface-colored band slows down until it covers the whole block, then snaps away each 1.44s loop. Fix: drop after:-translate-x-full and give fw-shimmer 'from { transform: translateX(-100%) }' (same as fw-progress). notes: 2026-10-08 review fail by reviewer: Acceptance 1-8 are all present in the text and the 3 diagrams pass mapgrain validate. Fail because the Safe rules contradict each other and can freeze funds: (1) 'Guard allows only the factory and receivers as targets' blocks Safe self-calls, so addOwner/swapOwner/changeThreshold/setGuard/enableModule are impossible; this contradicts 'owner changes applied on every chain', and since refundAuthority is immutable in the factory, losing keys over time freezes all held funds (overpay, late, expired, missed settle) forever. (2) The same Guard blocks calls to the Delay module (queue and the cancel path target the Delay contract), and it lets owners call refund/recover directly on receivers, so the 24-48 h delay is not enforced. Safe 1.4.1 Guards do not check module transactions. Fix: Guard allows self-calls (or a named allowlist of Safe admin selectors) and the Delay module; it rejects direct refund/recover/settle-after-deadline selectors so they only run through the Delay; setPaused and setExecutor stay direct. (3) contracts-workflow refund and recover nodes say 'the same Safe transaction calls Factory.deploy first'; that needs MultiSend, which is a delegatecall the Guard blocks. Say two transactions, or allow MultiSendCallOnly by address. Cosmetic: PLAN.md line 520 and the contracts-workflow 'missed' node still say 'settle window'; the Phase 5 Gate line does not mention the real-receiver vs predict check (the Done-list does); state how the factory's first executor is set (constructor arg changes the CREATE2 address).

The 3 diagrams validate. Still fails: the rule 'refund, recover and post-deadline settle run only through the Delay module' is not true as written. The same 3 owners the delay should slow down can skip it instantly: (1) a direct MultiSendCallOnly batch whose inner call is receiver.refund(attacker): the Guard sees only to=MultiSendCallOnly, operation=delegatecall, unless it decodes the batch; (2) a direct self-call setGuard(0) or disableModule, then a direct refund; (3) a direct Delay.setTxCooldown(0) or setTxExpiration, since the Delay is an allowed target. This is the blind-signing case (signers tricked into one malicious transaction) that the delay and the hash check exist for. Fix in AGENTS.md, PLAN.md and the security-keys node: the Guard decodes MultiSendCallOnly batches and applies the same target and function rules to each inner call; Safe admin changes (owners, threshold, guard, modules, fallback handler) and Delay settings go through the Delay too (rotation still works, after 24-48 h); direct transactions are allowed only for setPaused, setExecutor (harmless: the executor can only pay the recipient), queueing on the Delay and cancel (setTxNonce). tasks.behavior: Fix the Codex review findings: JWKS key age, signer only on enabled chains, confirm externally settled intents, guarded intent updates
acceptance: A withdrawn JWKS key stops verifying after MaxKeyAge and a failed refresh never extends that age; the signer drops chains no longer enabled, skips a round when the enabled list can't be read, works only on intents of chains it serves, and bounds each attempt so a hanging RPC stalls nothing

A settlement is confirmed only when the receiver is settled at the finalized block (a settle dropped by a reorg is sent again); a receiver settled outside our signer, or after the deadline by the refund authority, is confirmed and booked; paid needs the second RPC's finalized balance; retry and refuse only update an intent still in the status they loaded
notes: 2026-10-09 review pass by subagent: All four fixes are correct. Backend test (go test -race) and e2e pass. Each new test fails when its fix is reverted in a scratch copy: TestWithdrawnKeyStopsVerifying (withdrawn key still accepted), TestExternallySettledIntentIsConfirmed (23514 settlement_intents_sent_check), TestStaleAttemptDoesNotOverwriteAConfirmedIntent (moved to refused), TestSignerSkipsChainsItDoesNotServe (no RPC for chain 31337). A scratch test also checked the Privy-unreachable fallback and that 50 concurrent stale requests make 1 fetch under -race; both pass. Notes, none blocking: (1) auth.go:103,109-111 sets fetchedAt before a refresh that fails, so a withdrawn key is trusted up to about 2x MaxKeyAge if Privy is down at the refresh. The fallback has no test in the repo. (2) architecture.md:122 says the refund authority settling after the deadline confirms the intent. That only holds if the signer did not look at the intent between the deadline and that settle. Otherwise service.go:133-134 refuses it first, and a refused intent is never looked at again, so the payout stays unbooked. R-30 says pending only, so this is a gap in the doc wording, not in the fix. (3) cmd/signer/main.go:61-80 (skip the round when the enabled list fails, drop disabled chains) is not covered by any test; it was checked by reading the code. The loop is one goroutine, so it cannot race with Run. A 'sent' intent on a disabled chain is not reconciled until the chain is enabled again. (4) The 00005 Down migration fails if a confirmed row without tx fields exists. That is normal for a constraint that gets stricter on Down. (5) retry/refuse do not check RowsAffected, so a stale call does nothing and reports no error. That is fine, and settle() sets in.status='sent' before reconcile (service.go:182), so the sent-path retry still matches.

Every new test fails with its fix removed (checked in a scratch copy): confirmIfFinal->confirm fails TestSettlesAPaidInvoiceOnce, TestExternallySettledIntentIsConfirmed, TestSettleDroppedByReorgIsSentAgain; settler->refuse fails TestAfterTheDeadline...; BalanceFrom at head fails TestPaidNeedsTheSecondRPCToAgree; old auth.go fails TestFailedRefreshDoesNotExtendKeyAge; no attempt timeout fails TestHangingRPCDoesNotStallTheSigner (stuck). Finality: confirm() has one caller, confirmIfFinal (service.go:247-253), so nothing books before settled() is true at the finalized tag. If the settle is not final yet, the intent stays pending or sent and is checked again next round. A reorged settle is not settled at latest and has no receipt, so reconcile resends the saved bytes, or retries if its nonce was taken. I found no new state where a sent intent is stuck forever. The old one remains: a saved tx priced under a doubled base fee errors every round (the known no-fee-bump limit). eth_call at the finalized tag answered at the finalized block on Base Sepolia (lag 458), Arbitrum Sepolia (3746) and Tempo (1) public RPCs. Arc RPCs were blocked from here (HTTP 1009), but Arc finalized = latest (R-28). Anvil runs with --slots-in-an-epoch 1 (finalized = latest-2). An empty eth_call answer counted as 0 can't make an invoice paid; with booked > 0 it also blocks expiry. Notes, none blocking: (a) service.go:139-141, after the deadline: if the refund authority refunds instead of settling, the intent stays pending forever and is checked about hourly. Any intent refused earlier with 'deadline passed?' stays refused, because no migration moves it back. (b) An intent waiting for the authority backs off up to 1h, so its settle is booked up to about 1h late. (c) A sent settle whose deadline passed is resent once and reverts, costing gas, before the intent goes back to pending. (d) auth.go:99-104: while Privy is unreachable, a known key keeps verifying past MaxKeyAge (it fails open), with one retry a minute. This is the documented choice.

2026-10-09 Open notes from the final review: after the deadline a refund (not settle) by the authority leaves the intent pending forever (checked hourly); a sent settle past the deadline is resent once and reverts; no fee bumping for stuck txs.

notes: 2026-10-09 review fail by reviewer: FAIL. Defect: apps/backend/internal/privy/privy.go:43 sends a fixed privy-idempotency-key per profile. Privy docs (docs.privy.io/api-reference/idempotency-keys) say wallet create caches 4xx AND 5xx responses for the key's 24h lifetime and replays them; a new key is needed to retry. So one transient 5xx (or a 4xx such as a not-yet-visible user) during signup (R-32) blocks that profile's wallet for 24h: every retry, including the SDK's own 2 retries, replays the cached error. The key adds no safety: external_id is documented 'Unique per app. No two wallets in the same app can share an external_id' (docs.privy.io/wallets/wallets/external-ids), and the lookup-after-failed-create already covers the race. Fix: drop the idempotency key (line 43), update accept 1 and docs/backend/architecture.md:75, and add a fake case where the first create returns 500 and the next call succeeds (fake should replay cached errors per idempotency key, or assert no key is sent). Non-blocking: (1) privy.go:56 lists by external_id only; add UserID: privyUserID so a wallet owned by another Privy user is never returned (a caller passing a wrong user then fails closed via the create conflict instead of getting someone else's wallet). (2) List hides archived wallets by default (include_archived=false), so an archived profile wallet makes ProfileWallet fail with the create error; fine while nothing archives. (3) privy_test.go:150 only proves a failed lookup is reported, not 'create fails and lookup finds nothing returns the create error'. (4) The fake answers duplicate external_id with 409 (privy_test.go:65), which the SDK retries twice with backoff (tests take 1.3-1.5s); real Privy's duplicate code is undocumented; outcome is the same since any create error falls back to lookup. (5) SDK DefaultClientOptions reads PRIVY_APP_ID/SECRET/API_BASE_URL/API_CUSTOM_HEADERS from env; explicit options override the first three, CUSTOM_HEADERS would still apply (outside internal/config). OK: UUID profile ids are valid external_ids (36 chars, [0-9a-f-]); fallback cannot mask auth errors (lookup fails the same way) and can only return the wallet created for this external_id; SDK logging defaults to LogLevelNone, no header/body logs; timeouts come from ctx plus 10m response-header timeout; go.mod only adds lines, golang.org/x/crypto stays v0.55.0 (MVS picks max over SDK's v0.41.0), go mod tidy -diff clean, go mod verify ok; vet with e2e,privylive tags fine; no interface added, API URL injected, fits rules.md. tasks.behavior: The backend records every token transfer in and out of profile wallets and serves them as a transactions list and a balance history
acceptance: The worker records every enabled-token transfer to or from each profile wallet on each enabled chain, with the same finality and reorg rules as deposits; GET /v1/profiles/{id}/transactions lists them newest first with cursor pages; GET /v1/profiles/{id}/balance-history returns points that end at the current finalized balance; tested on Anvil
openapi.yaml and docs/backend/api.md describe both routes; both are owner-only like the other profile routes; the dashboard chart and Transactions page are built in the app redesign task that follows
notes: 2026-10-10 review fail by reviewer: FAIL. (1) Not fixed, blocking: watcher/wallet.go:32 scans wallet transfers only in enabled tokens, but watcher.go start() holds the scan at the oldest detected wallet_transfers row of any token. If an operator disables a token while one of its wallet transfers is still detected (likely for any active token, since finality takes minutes to hours), that row is never confirmed or reorged, and the chain's scan start stays at its block forever. Every poll then rescans from that block to latest, a range that grows without bound and also slows deposits on that chain. Reproduced on Anvil: after the token was disabled and 80 blocks mined, the row stayed detected, start()=3 while last_finalized_block=81. Deposits do not have this problem because invoices are scanned whatever their token's enabled flag. Suggested fix: keep reading the tokens of detected rows until those rows settle (for a disabled token, update only rows that already exist), or settle such rows another way, then add an Anvil test. (2) Fixed: balance/history.go day buckets were (previous 00:00, 00:00], so a transfer at exactly 00:00:00 UTC counted in the previous day's received/sent and end balance. Changed both comparisons to >= so a day is [00:00, next 00:00). history_test now mints today's transfer at exactly 00:00 UTC via evm_setNextBlockTimestamp. It fails without the fix (balances [0 100000000 75000000 75000000], want [0 100000000 70000000 75000000]). (3) Process, not fixed: F072 acceptance 2 was narrowed to drop the dashboard chart and Transactions page 'to the app redesign task that follows', but no such task is queued. The owner should confirm and add it. (4) Minor: start() and pending() filter wallet_transfers by chain_id and status='detected' on every poll with no index, the same as chain_transfers, but this table grows with every wallet transfer. A partial index on (chain_id, block_number) WHERE status = 'detected' would keep these reads cheap. Checked and OK: reorg handling (rows marked reorged before inserts, a re-mined copy gets a new row, live unique index), confirmation only at or below the finalized block, the start rule and the 64-block window, wallet-to-wallet transfers recorded once per side, big.Int with no floats, cursor (block_time, id) stable with ties (tested at every page size), owner-only through profileScoped (both routes in profileRoutes), days/limit/cursor validation (400/422), no SQL injection (the table name is a constant), no N+1 queries, history bounded by days. The clamp of negative balances to 0 is a display rule, documented in openapi, api.md and a code comment, and justified by Arc gas and native sends that log no Transfer. File placement follows docs/backend/rules.md. Ran: pnpm --filter @forwend/backend test (pass before and after the fix); verify F072 passed all 9 checks.

2026-10-10 review pass by reviewer: PASS on re-review. All earlier findings are resolved. (1) Disabled token: wallets() now also reads tokens that still have detected rows on the chain, and transfers() counts a disabled token's log only when it matches an existing detected row (same block hash and log index). Checked: such a row confirms once final, and the scan start goes back to 64 blocks below finalized (TestDetectedTransferOfADisabledTokenStillConfirms). In a scratch Anvil test (deleted afterwards), a disabled token's detected row whose block was replaced is marked reorged; its re-mined copy is not recorded, as the docs say for new transfers of a disabled token; and the start went back to finalized+1-64 (67 vs 130). A token row cannot be removed while wallet_transfers rows reference it (FK, no ON DELETE), so that case cannot happen. The filter never applies to enabled tokens. For a disabled token it skips only rows that would be new (a re-mined copy, or a reorged row coming back), which matches the documented rule, so no update of an existing detected row is lost. (2) Partial index wallet_transfers_detected (chain_id, block_number) WHERE status = 'detected' was added. (3) F079 and R-39 now cover the dashboard chart and Transactions page; F079 depends on F072. (4) My earlier fix holds: history day buckets are [00:00, next 00:00), and history_test mints a transfer at exactly 00:00 UTC. Ran: pnpm --filter @forwend/backend test, all packages pass. Verify passed at 10:12:39Z (9 checks).

tasks.behavior: The web app reads and writes API data through Redux Toolkit and RTK Query, with the same screens and refresh behavior
acceptance: A store per tab and per signed-in user (store/store.ts makeStore, providers/store-provider.tsx) holds only the RTK Query cache; shared/api/api-slice.ts sets the base URL and Privy token; profiles, balances and activity inject their endpoints from their features; useLoad and the hand-written fetch client are gone.

Balances and activity read again every 15 s while the tab is visible and when it comes back; query arguments include the profile, so another profile's data never shows; a new profile joins the cached list without a refetch; a user change or ended session gives a fresh empty store; amounts stay exact strings.
Same screens and copy: lint, typecheck, unit, build, e2e and the live sign-in suite pass.
notes: 2026-10-10 review fail by reviewer: Cross-user cache leak when the Privy session ends without the Sign out button. apps/web/src/screens/app-shell/app-shell.tsx:46 caches POST /v1/me under one key (undefined) for every user, and resetApiState runs only in signOut (app-shell.tsx:63-67). StoreProvider lives in app/(app)/layout.tsx, which also wraps /sign-in, so the store survives the redirect. Scenario: A's session expires or is revoked (Privy sets authenticated=false), the shell redirects to /sign-in, the signUp and balances entries stay for keepUnusedDataFor (60 s). B signs in in the same tab within 60 s: useSignUpQuery(undefined) finds a fulfilled entry and sends no request (no refetchOnMountOrArgChange), so B sees A's profiles and A's cached balances. signUp never polls, so A's list stays for B's whole session; failed balance polls keep A's amounts in currentData. Reproduced with RTK 2.12.0 core: initiate, unsubscribe, initiate again gives 1 request and A's data. The old code kept profiles in AppShell state, which reset on unmount. Fix: clear the cache whenever authenticated becomes false (e.g. an effect in StoreProvider or AppShell calling apiSlice.util.resetApiState), or key signUp by Privy user.id; add a test. Everything else checked OK: per-profile keys with currentData and the keyed ActivityList remount; 15 s polling with skipPollingIfUnfocused plus refetchOnFocus; token per request via prepareHeaders; idempotency key per form; the active profile falls back to profiles[0], so no error flash; per-tab store; amounts stay strings; layout follows structure.md. Non-blocking: A->B->A within 60 s shows A's cached balances (with their timestamp) for up to 15 s before the next poll; the window focus event adds a refetch the old code did not make; one poll can still fire right after the tab hides, because polling.ts:105 reads the focus state from when the poll was scheduled. typecheck and the 17 unit tests pass.

2026-10-10 review pass by reviewer: Fix holds. StoreProvider swaps the store with setState during render, guarded by owned.userId !== userId, so React re-runs StoreProvider before any child renders and no child reads the old store; no loop (the second pass matches). Privy (3.45.0 source) sets user and authenticated in the same batch on logout, token removal, login, session restore and cross-tab sync, so AppShell's signUp arg turns to skipToken in the same render as the swap. Scratch-copy probe under StrictMode (scratchpad only, repo untouched): load -> A gives 1 POST /v1/me with A's token and balances polling on the new store; logout gives 0 requests in 300 ms (old store's polling unsubscribed on unmount); B then gets a new POST /v1/me with B's token and B's data. Store count: 2 on mount (StrictMode init), +1 per user change. Null -> A while Privy loads is harmless: queries are skipped until ready, so nothing is lost and no extra request goes out. store-provider.test.tsx fails on the pre-fix provider (expected { profiles: [] } to be undefined) and passes with the fix. typecheck passes; 18 unit tests pass. Earlier points still hold: profileId in query args with currentData and the keyed ActivityList; LIVE_QUERY 15 s polling plus focus refetch; token read per request in prepareHeaders; one idempotency key per form; profiles[0] fallback, so no error flash. Non-blocking: (1) RTK's useQuerySubscription keeps the subscription lookup of the store it first mounted with. A direct A -> B change without passing through null leaves AppShell's signUp uninitialized (spinner until reload; no data leak). Privy always goes through null, so this cannot happen today. After the first swap the same lookup also adds one extra signUp subscription (no extra request). (2) D-47 in PROJECT.md says the cache reset on sign-out comes from the library; it now comes from the store swap. The profiles-api.test name 'forgets it all on sign-out' tests resetApiState, which app code no longer uses. (3) docs/web/structure.md still lists store/hooks.ts as an option ('as needed'), which is fine.

notes: 2026-10-10 review pass by reviewer: Pass. (1) BEFORE INSERT trigger numbering: the profile row lock is the first lock the insert takes, so creates for one profile take turns; any failed insert (CHECK, unique key, idempotency race) rolls the counter back with the statement, so no gaps. No deadlock path: only ensureWallet also locks profiles (FOR UPDATE, then profile_wallets), the worker/signer never lock profiles, FK checks take FOR KEY SHARE which does not conflict. No INSERT ... ON CONFLICT on invoices exists; a future one would burn a number when it skips a row. Backfill by (created_at, id) is tested; Down is covered by the existing DownTo(0) test. (2) Separate invoices_number trigger: fires after invoices_guard (name order), IS DISTINCT FROM covers number and all six detail columns, status transitions still pass (existing transition test runs on all migrations). (3) List: profile_id filter, owner-only route, limit 1-100 (422), bad cursor 422, number cursor is unique per profile so pages never skip or repeat. Validation, %q hash over new fields, public GET without client, owner create/list with client, settlementTxHash from the unique confirmed intent, activity txHash, openapi/api.md: correct. Old idempotency keys would 409 after the hash change; acceptable since nothing is deployed. Mutation check: replacing the counter with max(number)+1 makes TestCreateNumbersInvoicesAtOnce fail 3/3, so the concurrency test is meaningful. pnpm --filter @forwend/backend test passes. Follow-up (pre-existing, not F084): settlement.reconcile confirms a sent intent when the receiver is settled without checking that our tx did it, so settlementTxHash can name a reverted or never-mined settle if the refund authority settled after our late send; ledger amounts are unaffected, and api.md/openapi then overstate the null case.

tasks.behavior: Chain reads switch providers and slow down instead of failing the round
acceptance: Each enabled chain has a pool of every Infura key plus the public RPCs (public only when INFURA_API_KEYS is empty); a call that gets 429, a 5xx, a rate-limit JSON-RPC error or a timeout moves to the next endpoint at once and rests the failing one with exponential backoff and jitter; the two independent hosts of D-15 are kept, a failed second host is replaced by another host; each endpoint is paced by a configurable request rate

eth_getLogs halves its block range on a 429 or a too-large error down to a floor and grows back after successes; a worker round survives an endpoint going 429 mid-round; tests use a fault-injecting JSON-RPC proxy in front of Anvil (429s, 5xx, timeouts, rate-limit errors) and show reads move to the next endpoint and recover, and a public-only pool works

Only non-idempotent call is eth_sendRawTransaction of already-signed bytes (settle saved before send; reconcile tolerates 'already known'; deploy resend is idempotent), so re-sending to another endpoint never signs a new nonce. Batches: a rate limit on any element re-sends the whole read-only batch. D-15: at each pick the second skips the primary's current host and waits/fails rather than share it. Gap (second may later hit a host that served the primary's logs) is acceptable: it already existed across rounds with the old re-pick-after-error Dial, needs an outage of an earlier-listed host the liar can't cause, and settle still needs the real on-chain balance; follow-up only if D-15 must hold per deposit (record the confirming host). Adaptive range: retries same lo with half span, both scans re-queried, no gap/overlap, floor 50 then error, one DB transaction after the loop so the cursor never moves on a partial scan. No URL in errors/logs (url.Error stripped, endpoint names host#pos). chainId checked before first use, wrong endpoints never used. RPC_RATE_PER_SECOND required in LoadAPI/worker/signer, INFURA_API_KEYS may be empty; .env.example and architecture.md match chains.json. FIXED (pool.go): requests queued on an endpoint's pace slot were still sent after it began resting, and each failure doubled the rest; a probe of 8 queued requests gave 8 failures and an 82 s rest from one 429 burst. Now a queued request re-picks when its endpoint rests, and a failure during an existing rest is not counted again. tasks.behavior: Settlements estimate gas on a node that sees the receiver and never lose a successful settle
acceptance: After a deploy the signer estimates settle gas only when the estimating node returns the receiver's code (waits briefly, else retries the round), keeps a safety margin, and takes the nonce consistently (the higher of the node's pending nonce and the signer's last used nonce); a settle whose receipt succeeded and emitted the receiver's settle event is confirmed with its hash and is never re-queued or cleared because a later read at latest says not settled; settled reads use the receipt block or finalized, not latest

Anvil tests with a stale-read proxy: a node that has not seen the deploy yet does not produce a low gas estimate; a mined successful settle followed by a stale not-settled read keeps its hash and is booked once; the F099 refund-authority case still records no hash
notes: 2026-10-10 review pass by reviewer: Traced every sent-intent transition in reconcile/unmined/confirmIfFinal/settle. No double send (the same signed bytes are resent, the contract's settled flag guards), no double booking (confirm checks the status FOR UPDATE), no premature confirm (every confirm needs settled() at the finalized block, and our receipt's block <= finalized). A retry happens only after a revert or once our nonce is used at finalized, so the old settle can never mine later. The log check is exact: status 1 plus a log from the receiver's address with the Settled topic0. Only the clone emits from that address, so the receipt check also catches a status-1 call to an address without code. Nonce: max(pending, deploy+1, max saved nonce with tx_hash +1). A saved but unsent settle is counted, so no reuse; it can leave a temporary gap until the same round resends it (later intents wait up to ReceiptWait). F099: TestSettledByTheRefundAuthority (reverted and never mined) still has no hash, and the st.Settled path is unchanged. TestNonceTakenByAnotherTransaction now expects sent until final: justified, because taken is decided at finalized so a lagging receipt read can't drop our settle. Gas, measured on an Anvil fork of Base Sepolia with real USDC and the real factory: settle used 135,632 gas (estimate 139,592) paying a fresh wallet and 118,532 paying a funded one; floor+1/5 = 150,000 covers it. Fixed: the SettleGasFloor comment now records this and says the floor does not cover Arbitrum's L1 data gas; re-verified with the same proofs (9/9 passed). Residual, non-blocking: (a) stuck case (no receipt, settled at finalized, our nonce used there) needs the executor key used outside the signer; it logs slog.Warn every round with no reason or backoff saved, so it shows only in logs; (b) a stale estimate on Arbitrum can still run out of gas: it reverts, is retried, and only wastes gas. EstimateGasAtBlock(deploy block) would close this; (c) a saved settle that can never be sent (fee cap below the base fee, no fee bumping) now blocks later settles on that chain. Ran pnpm --filter @forwend/backend test (-race) and e2e: both exit 0.

tasks.behavior: The API serves 10k users without hammering the chain or the database
acceptance: Balance reads share one chain read per (chain, wallet, finalized block) with a short cache and request coalescing behind a small interface that a Redis implementation could replace later; balance-history reuses it; ledger_transactions gets an index on invoice_id; the DB pool size is configurable; per-user rate limits answer 429 with Retry-After; the web backs off on 429

A load test in the repo (no paid service) simulating many signed-in users polling every 15 s reports p50/p95 and RPC calls per second before and after; the numbers are recorded in docs/backend with the deployment model (stateless API replicas behind a load balancer, one worker and one signer)
notes: 2026-10-10 review pass by reviewer: PASS after one fix. Balance cache: key covers chain, token, wallet and block; errors not kept; first caller's cancel does not fail waiters (WithoutCancel, deadline kept); memory bounded by keys per minute. Migrate strips only pool_ params. Web 429 backoff cannot loop; tests meaningful. Transport keeps dial/TLS timeouts. Load test compares like with like. FIXED: per-IP limit trusted the client's X-Forwarded-For (Next's rewrite does not set it), so honest payers shared one bucket and a forger was never limited; removed the per-IP limit and the one-implementation limiter interface, public routes are to be limited at the edge (api.md, D-72). tasks.behavior: The signer replaces a stuck settle with a higher fee, estimates gas at the deploy block, and flags settles it cannot resolve
acceptance: A sent settle not mined after a set time is re-signed with the same nonce and a higher fee (capped), so later settles on that chain are not blocked; settle gas is estimated at the deploy receipt block where the node supports it (Arbitrum L1 data gas covered); an intent that cannot be resolved (no receipt, receiver settled, our nonce used at finalized) gets a stored reason, slows its retries and shows in an ops query; Anvil tests cover a stuck low-fee settle being replaced and booked once
notes: 2026-10-10 review pass by reviewer: PASS. settlement tests -race x3 no flakes. Saved before send for settle and every replacement; replacement guarded by status='sent' AND tx_hash=old plus the advisory lock; confirm books once (FOR UPDATE, unique index) with the mined receipt's hash; a new nonce is signed only via retry when the nonce is spent; replaced_hashes cleared only then. Same nonce, gas, calldata; fee bump max(current, ceil(9x/8)) in big.Int. Booking still waits for finality and Settled at finalized (D-45). Ops SQL planned against migrated schema; 00012 down reverses up. Fixed after review: a revert at the deploy block no longer falls back to latest; stall wait documented as 2 min doubling; a describing comment removed. Re-verified 9 checks.
